texts: Each Keeper tends a station alone.
When a Keeper trains an apprentice, the Keeper and the apprentice tend the station together.
During high-wraith weeks, two Keepers tend the Stilllight Lantern together.
A night shift begins at sundown.
A Keeper checks the lantern at midnight.
A Keeper checks the lantern at the third watch.

fields.sentence: Each Keeper tends a station alone.

q2_gaps: the adverbial 'alone' in its solitary / unaccompanied sense: it is not a how-manner adverb proper, not one of the barred adverb classes (duration, sequence, scope, degree), not a depictive state of the subject, and not one of the listed focus particles ('only / just / solely'), so no routing is specified
review.notes: The bare-'each' universal, the Skolem-function event, the dependent existential `(sk_station $x)` with its own typing, the 1.0/0.9 rule TV and the QuantifierPhrase companion all match the instruction set exactly, and `keeper` correctly stays a plain kind (referring use, so no agent-nominalization capability). The one debatable atom is `(Manner (sk_tend $x) alone)` — defensible as a how-adverb, but it is the gap recorded above.

fields.sentence: When a Keeper trains an apprentice, the Keeper and the apprentice tend the station together.
parse: (: train_tend_rule (Implication (And (Member $t train) (Agent $t $k) (Theme $t $a) (Member $k keeper) (Member $a apprentice)) (And (Member (sk_tend $t) tend) (Agent (sk_tend $t) $k) (Agent (sk_tend $t) $a) (Theme (sk_tend $t) sk_station_1) (During (sk_tend $t) $t))) (STV 1.0 0.9))

review.notes: Bare "when P, Q" with indefinite participants correctly routes to the whenever machinery (plain-variable premises, Skolem-function consequent, During link, STV 1.0 0.9, no QuantifierPhrase), and bare "together" on the coordinated subject correctly yields one tend event with two Agent atoms; the definite "the station" sits as a top-level typed constant as the bell/dog example does.

fields.sentence: During high-wraith weeks, two Keepers tend the Stilllight Lantern together.

q1_issues.issue: The 'during' PP is encoded as (Time sk_tend_1 high_wraith_week), but the instruction set reserves the head During for exactly the words during/while/throughout, and a Time filler must be a structured calendar term or a deictic/named-time constant — high_wraith_week is neither, it is a compound common-noun KIND the parse itself puts in a class slot at statement 0.

q2_gaps: 'during' + a bare-plural non-calendar period noun ('during high-wraith weeks') framing a habitual clause: During requires a reified eventuality as its outer argument, Time requires a calendar term or a deictic/named constant, and the frequency machinery (Every / TimesPer / named slot) requires a calendar slot or a stated period — so a recurring described period has no licensed carrier
review.notes: The rest is as specified: counted plural to group + Cardinality 2, 'together' consumed as the collective marker so the group event stands alone with no per-member rule, 'the Stilllight Lantern' as one name symbol with its Name plus the kind atom read off the kind word inside the name, Theme by the unclear-case default, and the high_wraith_week head genus with the modifier unexposed.

issues.reason: This is graceful improvisation in gap territory, not a defect: a bare period symbol in the Time slot has direct precedent (day-parts as bare symbols, '(Time e morning)', and a fiscal period 'else the bare constant first_quarter'), the atom is true of the sentence's content and over-asserts nothing, and the During route the reviewer points to is structurally unavailable — During takes two reified eventualities, which a bare-plural period kind supplies only by wrongly individuating one particular week.

gaps_confirmed: 'during' + a bare-plural non-calendar period noun framing a habitual clause has no licensed carrier: During needs two reified eventualities, Time is specified for calendar terms and deictic/named constants, and Every/TimesPer need a named calendar slot or a stated period/rate.
new_gaps: Whether a period KIND symbol may fill a Time slot is unstated, and here the same symbol also sits in a class position in (Inheritance high_wraith_week week); the instruction set fixes the individual/class discipline for Member vs Inheritance but says nothing about one symbol serving as both a kind and a time filler.

The recurrence carried by the plural 'weeks' is not recoverable from a single Time atom, and no frequency carrier fits a period named by description rather than by calendar slot, stated cycle or rate.
adjudication.notes: The rest is as specified: counted plural to group + Cardinality 2, 'together' consumed as the collective marker so the group event stands alone with no per-member rule, the Stilllight Lantern as one name symbol with its Name plus the kind atom read off the name-internal kind word, and no status atom on the habitual.

fields.sentence: A night shift begins at sundown.

review.notes: Matches the instruction set's own "The harvest begins in September" pattern exactly: Patient on the intransitive begin-subject, no tense atom (no TODAY and no lexically future adjunct, so the futurate rule cannot fire), and "sundown" as a bare day-part constant on Time. The compound is correctly fused with its head genus emitted and the noun modifier "night" correctly not exposed; indefinite "a" under a verbal predicate correctly mints a witness rather than a generic.

fields.sentence: A Keeper checks the lantern at midnight.

review.notes: The indefinite subject is correctly a witness rather than a generic rule, the bare simple present correctly takes no status atom (no futurate evidence, no Ongoing marker), and 'keeper' in referring position rightly gets no (can keep) capability. 'midnight' as a bare Time constant follows the noon/dawn/dusk day-part pattern rather than (Hour 0), a boundary the instruction set does not name explicitly.

fields.sentence: A Keeper checks the lantern at the third watch.

review.notes: "At the third watch" as the bare time constant third_watch follows the first_quarter precedent (an ordinally-named period with no year stays a bare constant) and correctly avoids During, licensed only for during/while/throughout. The indefinite "A Keeper" with a verbal predicate is a witness rather than a generic rule, checks takes Theme as an evaluate-only object, and the bare simple present correctly gets no status atom.

q1_issues.issue: The verbal clause "ends" is never reified as an event; the instruction set's direct parallel — "The harvest begins in September" → a begin event with the harvest as Patient plus a Time atom and no tense — reifies the boundary verb, while the interval End head is introduced for "from X to / until Y" framing rather than for a boundary verb's own clause.

review.notes: Two passages pull against each other here: the harvest/survey futurate example reifies the boundary verb, while the light-verb-over-event-noun and interval-End passages could be read as licensing a flat (End sk_shift_1 dawn). Omitting the tense atom is correct either way (no TODAY, unanchored adjunct).

issues.reason: 'The shift ends at dawn' is a verbal clause, so *Two kinds of clause* reifies an event, and the instruction set's own twin sentences settle it — 'the survey begins at dawn' / 'The harvest begins in September' are parsed as a reified begin event with the subject as Patient plus a Time atom and no tense — while Start/End stay pinned to from/to/until/since framing, as the 'When did X stop V-ing?' dual-storage note states outright (interval End from 'until <date>' versus a reified boundary event from the verb).

adjudication.defect_summary: Compliant form: (Member sk_end_1 end) (Patient sk_end_1 sk_shift_1) (Member sk_shift_1 shift) (Time sk_end_1 dawn) — 'dawn' is a licensed day-part constant on Time — with no tense atom (bare present, unanchored adjunct, no TODAY) and no (End sk_shift_1 dawn) beside it, since one fact takes one head.
adjudication.notes: The Intervals section names only the from/to/until/since wordings and never states the boundary against a boundary verb's own clause, so the flat-End reading is an understandable misread of a covered construction — an explicit line there would close it. Omitting the tense atom was correct under either reading.
